sentences.zh: 」丁丑，命學士院、講院、秘書監、司天臺、著作局、閣門、通進、拱衛、直武器署等官，凡直宮中，午前許退。

translations.literal: " On dingchou officials of the Hanlin Academy, Lecture Institute, Secretariat Directorate, Directorate of Astronomy, Compilation Bureau, Gate Office, Memorial Processing Office, Palace Guard, Direct Weapons Office, and the like—all who kept palace duty—were permitted to withdraw before noon.
translations.idiomatic: " On dingchou officials of the Hanlin Academy, Lecture Institute, Secretariat Directorate, Directorate of Astronomy, Compilation Bureau, Gate Office, Memorial Processing Office, Palace Guard, Direct Weapons Office, and the like—all on palace duty—were permitted to leave before noon.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚辰朔，詔曰：「豺未祭獸，不許採捕。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on gengchen the new moon, an edict said: "Before the jackal has sacrificed to the beasts, hunting and capture are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the gengchen new moon, an edict said, "Before the jackal has sacrificed to the beasts, hunting and capture are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 冬月，雪尺以上，不許用網及速撒海，恐盡獸類。

translations.literal: In winter, when snow is more than a foot deep, nets and the susahai seine are forbidden, lest the beasts be wiped out."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, when snow is more than a foot deep, nets and the susahai dragnet are forbidden, lest game be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 」歲星晝見。

translations.literal: " Jupiter was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: " Jupiter appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 壬午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On renwu Venus was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以臨潢尹僕散守中等為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: On jiawu Linhuang intendant Pusan Shouzhong and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on New Year’s Day.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Linhuang Intendant Pusan Shouzhong and others were sent to congratulate Song on New Year’s Day.

sentences.zh: 丙申，夏國遣使問起居。

translations.literal: On bingshen Western Xia sent envoys to inquire after the emperor’s health.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Western Xia sent envoys to inquire after the emperor’s health.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以曹王永功為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On wuxu Prince Cao Yonggong was made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Prince Cao Yonggong was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以禮部員外郎移剌履為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: On renyin Ministry of Rites outer-section officer Yila Lü was made Goryeo birthday envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Ministry of Rites Outer-Section Officer Yila Lü was sent as Goryeo birthday envoy.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午，以皇孫金源郡王麻達葛判大興尹，進封原王。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on wuwu, the imperial grandson Jin-yuan Prince Madage was made acting Daxing intendant and advanced to Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, the imperial grandson Jinyuan Prince Madage was made acting intendant of Daxing and promoted to Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太白晝見，經天。

translations.literal: On jiazi Venus was seen in daytime and crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Venus appeared in daylight and crossed the meridian.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，左相完顏守道、左丞張汝弼、右丞粘割斡特剌、參知政事張汝霖坐擅增東宮諸皇孫食料，各削官一階。

translations.literal: On bingyin Left Chancellor Wanyan Shoudao, Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi, Right Vice Councillor Zhagewo Hutela, and Participation Councillor Zhang Rulin, for having on their own increased the Eastern Palace imperial grandsons’ rations, were each demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Left Chancellor Wanyan Shoudao, Left Vice Councillor Zhang Rubi, Right Vice Councillor Zhagewo Hutela, and Participation Councillor Zhang Rulin, for having on their own increased the Eastern Palace imperial grandsons’ rations, were each demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，制增留守、統軍、總管、招討、都轉運、府尹、轉運、節度使月俸。

translations.literal: On jiaxu regulations increased the monthly salaries of military commissioners, circuit commanders, grand marshals, pacification commissioners, transport commissioners, prefects, transport agents, and military governors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu regulations increased the monthly salaries of military commissioners, circuit commanders, grand marshals, pacification commissioners, transport commissioners, prefects, transport agents, and military governors.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「太尉守道論事止務從寬，犯罪罷職者多欲複用。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chancellors: "Grand Guardian Shoudao in discussing affairs always seeks leniency; many who were dismissed for crime he wishes to employ again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chancellors, "Grand Guardian Shoudao in discussing affairs always seeks leniency; many dismissed for crime he would employ again.

sentences.zh: 若懲其首惡，後來知畏，罪而複用，何以示戒。

translations.literal: If we punish the chief culprits, those who follow will know fear; to punish and then employ again—how can that serve as a warning?"
translations.idiomatic: Punish the chief culprits and those who follow will know fear; to punish and then employ again—how is that a warning?"

sentences.zh: 」是日，命範銅為「禮信之寶」，凡賜外方禮物，給信袋則用之。

translations.literal: " That day he ordered bronze cast for the "Treasure of Ritual and Trust"; whenever gifts were bestowed to foreign states and trust pouches were given, it was used.
translations.idiomatic: " That day he ordered bronze cast for the "Treasure of Ritual and Trust"; whenever gifts were sent abroad with a trust pouch, it was used.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上問宰臣曰：「原王大興行事如何？

translations.literal: On bingzi the emperor asked the chancellors: "How does the Prince of Yuan conduct affairs at Daxing?"
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor asked the chancellors, "How does the Prince of Yuan conduct affairs at Daxing?"

sentences.zh: 」右丞斡特剌對曰：「聞都人皆稱之。

translations.literal: " Right Vice Councillor Hutela replied: "I hear the capital people all praise him."
translations.idiomatic: " Right Vice Councillor Hutela replied, "I hear the people of the capital all praise him."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕令察於民間，鹹言見事甚明，予奪皆不失當，曹、豳二王弗能及也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I ordered inquiry among the people; all say he is very clear in seeing affairs, and in grant and denial never misses the mark—the Princes of Cao and Bin cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I ordered inquiry among the people; all say he sees affairs very clearly and in grant and denial never misses the mark—the Princes of Cao and Bin cannot match him.

sentences.zh: 又聞有女直人訴事，以女直語問之，漢人訴事，漢語問之。

translations.literal: I also hear that when a Jurchen came to plead a case he questioned him in Jurchen, and when a Han man pleaded he questioned him in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that when a Jurchen came to plead a case he questioned him in Jurchen, and when a Han man came he questioned him in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 大習不失本朝語為善，不習，則淳風將棄。

translations.literal: To be well versed and not lose the language of our dynasty is good; if we do not learn it, the plain customs will be cast away."
translations.idiomatic: To be well versed and not lose our dynasty’s language is good; if we do not learn it, our plain customs will be cast away."

sentences.zh: 」汝弼對曰：「不忘本者，聖人之道也。

translations.literal: " Rubi replied: "Not to forget one’s roots is the way of the sages."
translations.idiomatic: " Rubi replied, "Not to forget one’s roots is the way of the sages."

sentences.zh: 」斡特剌曰：「以西夏小邦，崇尚舊俗，獨能保國數百年。

translations.literal: " Hutela said: "Western Xia is a small state, yet by honoring its old customs alone it has kept its realm for several hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: " Hutela said, "Western Xia is a small state, yet by honoring its old customs alone it has kept its realm for several hundred years."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「事當任實，一事為偽則喪百真，故凡事莫如真實也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Affairs must rest on what is real; if one thing is false a hundred truths are lost—therefore in all things nothing is like being true."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Affairs must rest on what is real; if one thing is false a hundred truths are lost—therefore in all things nothing surpasses truth."

sentences.zh: 二十六年正月庚辰朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Year twenty-six, first month, on gengchen the new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six, on the gengchen new moon of the first month, congratulatory envoys arrived from Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，如長春宮春水。

translations.literal: On jiachen he went to Changchun Palace for the spring waters.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he went to Changchun Palace for the spring waters.

sentences.zh: 二月癸酉，還都。

translations.literal: Second month, on guiyou, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiyou, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「每季求仕人，問以疑難，令剖決之。

translations.literal: On yihai an edict said: "Each season seek men for office and question them on difficult points, ordering them to decide cases.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai an edict said, "Each season seek candidates for office and question them on difficult points, ordering them to decide cases.

sentences.zh: 其才識可取者，仍訪察政跡，如其言行相副，即加升用。

translations.literal: Those whose talent and judgment may be taken should still be investigated for their administrative record; if words and deeds match, promote and employ them at once."
translations.idiomatic: Those whose talent and judgment warrant use should still be investigated for their administrative record; if words and deeds match, promote and employ them at once."

sentences.zh: 」三月乙卯朔，萬春節，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: " Third month, on yimao the new moon, the Ten-Thousand Springs festival; Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month, on the yimao new moon, at the Ten-Thousand Springs festival congratulatory envoys came from Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以大理卿闕，上問誰可？

translations.literal: On dinghai the post of director of the Court of Judicial Review was vacant; the emperor asked who would do.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the directorate of the Court of Judicial Review was vacant; the emperor asked who would serve.

sentences.zh: 右丞粘割斡特剌言，前使部尚書唐括貢可，乃授以是職。

translations.literal: Right Vice Councillor Zhagewo Hutela said that former envoy-section minister Tangque Gong would do, and he was thereupon appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Councillor Zhagewo Hutela said former Envoy-Section Minister Tangque Gong would do, and he was appointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 己丑，尚書省擬奏除授，上曰：「卿等在省未嘗薦士，止限資級，安能得人？

translations.literal: On jichou the Secretariat drafted appointments for presentation; the emperor said: "You in the Secretariat have never recommended scholars, but only limit yourselves to rank and seniority—how can you get the right men?
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Secretariat drafted appointments for presentation; the emperor said, "You in the Secretariat have never recommended scholars, but only limit yourselves to rank and seniority—how can you get the right men?

sentences.zh: 古有布衣人相者，聞宋亦多用山東、河南流寓疏遠之人，皆不拘於貴近也。

translations.literal: In antiquity commoners were made chancellors; I hear Song also much employed men from Shandong and Henan, wanderers from afar, all without being bound to the noble and near."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity commoners were made chancellors; I hear Song also much employed men from Shandong and Henan, wanderers from afar, all without being bound to the noble and near."

sentences.zh: 以本朝境土之大，豈無其人，朕難遍知，卿又不舉。

translations.literal: With our dynasty’s territory so vast, can there be no such men? I cannot know them all, and you do not recommend them."
translations.idiomatic: With our dynasty’s territory so vast, can there be no such men? I cannot know them all, and you do not recommend them."

sentences.zh: 自古豈有終身為相者，外官三品以上，必有可用之人，但無故得進耳。

translations.literal: From antiquity has there ever been one who was chancellor for life? Among outer officials of the third rank and above there must be men who can serve—it is only that they have no path to advance."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity has anyone been chancellor for life? Among outer officials of the third rank and above there must be men fit to serve—it is only that they have no path to advance."

translations.idiomatic: ” Left Vice Director Zhang Rubi said: “Men in humble posts may have ability, but only trial will show it.

translations.idiomatic: ” Participation Councillor Cheng Hui said: “Local officials may be well spoken of, yet once they reach court they may fail in office—that is only another sort of culling.

translations.idiomatic: ” On guisi Xiangshan Temple was finished; he went there, named it Great Everlasting Peace, and granted two thousand mou of land, seven thousand chestnut trees, and twenty thousand strings of cash.

translations.idiomatic: He said: “Let them know something of past and present, and they will refuse to do evil.

translations.literal: You, a coarse fellow of the guards, could yet speak thus—I see it is beneficial; why hesitate to follow it?”
translations.idiomatic: A rough guardsman like you could say this—I see the good in it; why hold back from adopting it?”

translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on renzi, the Department of State Affairs reported regulations for bureau supervisors’ deficit compensation and exchange delivery, and the lateral-rank table.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「朕常日禦膳亦從減省，嘗有一公主至，至無餘膳可與，當直官皆目睹之。

translations.idiomatic: He said: “I already pare my daily meals; once when a princess arrived there was nothing left to set before her, and every officer on duty saw it.

sentences.zh: 若欲豐腆，雖日用五十羊亦不難矣！

translations.literal: If I wished abundance, even fifty sheep a day would not be hard!
translations.idiomatic: If I wanted plenty, fifty sheep a day would be easy enough!

sentences.zh: 然皆民之脂膏，不忍為也。

translations.literal: Yet it is all the people’s fat and marrow—I cannot bear to do it.
translations.idiomatic: But it is all wrung from the people’s substance—I will not do it.

sentences.zh: 監臨官惟知利己，不知其利自何而來？

translations.literal: Supervising officers know only to profit themselves—they do not know where their profit comes from?
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors think only of their own gain—do they know where that gain comes from?

sentences.zh: 朕嘗曆外任，稔知民間之事，想前代之君，雖享富貴，不知稼穡艱難者甚多，其失天下，皆由此也！

translations.literal: I have served in outer posts and am well acquainted with the people’s affairs; I think many rulers of former ages, though enjoying wealth and honor, did not know the hardship of farming—losing the realm was all from this!
translations.idiomatic: I have held posts in the provinces and know the people’s affairs well; many rulers of old, though rich and exalted, never learned how hard the harvest is—losing the realm always began there!

sentences.zh: 遼主聞民間乏食，謂何不食幹臘，蓋幼失師保之訓，及其即位，故不知民間疾苦也。

translations.literal: When the Liao ruler heard the people lacked food, he asked why they did not eat dried meat—having lost teachers and guardians in youth, when he took the throne he did not know the people’s sufferings.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor heard the people had no food, he asked why they did not eat jerky—he had lost his tutors in boyhood, and on taking the throne he knew nothing of popular hardship.

sentences.zh: 隨煬帝時，楊素專權行事，乃不慎委任之過也。

translations.literal: In Sui Yangdi’s time Yang Su wielded power alone—that was the fault of careless appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Yangdi, Yang Su acted as he pleased—that came of appointing men without care.

sentences.zh: 與正人同處，所知必正道，所聞必正言，不可不慎也。

translations.literal: To dwell with upright men means what one knows must be the right Way and what one hears must be right speech—this cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Keep company with upright men and what you learn will be the right Way and what you hear right words—this must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 今原王府官屬，當選純謹秉性正直者充，勿用有權術之人。

translations.literal: For Prince Yuan’s household staff now, choose those of pure, cautious, and upright character; do not employ men skilled in court intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: For Prince Yuan’s household staff, choose men who are pure, cautious, and upright in nature; do not use men versed in intrigue.

translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he went to Shou’an Palace.

translations.idiomatic: As the Department of State Affairs reported, the emperor said: “A recent memorial held that officials struck from the rolls for crime must not serve again—I find that wholly right.

sentences.zh: 如軍期急速，權可使用。

translations.literal: If military deadlines press, they may be used provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: When armies must move in haste, they may be used for the moment.

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，複用此輩，何以戒將來。

translations.literal: But today the realm is at peace; reusing such men—how will we warn the future.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm is at peace now; to put such men back in office—how will that warn those who come after?

translations.idiomatic: An edict said: “Measured against antiquity, present taxes are light—and whenever disaster strikes, remission is added.”

translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Censorate Grandee Prince Cao Yonggong left office, and Prince Bin Yongcheng became censorate grandee.

translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Right Vice Director Niange Watele became left vice director, and Participation Councillor Zhang Rulin right vice director.

translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai, the Department of State Affairs reported on hereditary mouke succession among the Sufen and Huli Gai; the emperor said: “They are a fierce people; our founding forebear neighbored them and fought bitterly for years before barely subduing them.

translations.idiomatic: Afterward they submitted and rebelled by turns; only under Mu and Kang did they accept our transforming rule.

translations.idiomatic: In recent times some have also been moved away.

translations.idiomatic: ” On jisi the emperor told the chief ministers: “Duke Huan of Qi was no more than a middling ruler, yet one Guan Zhong made him hegemon.

sentences.zh: 朕夙夜以思，惟恐失人。

translations.literal: I think day and night, fearing only to miss the right man.
translations.idiomatic: I brood on it day and night, fearing only that I shall miss the right man.

translations.literal: You and I are all old!
translations.idiomatic: You and I are growing old!

translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on renwu, pay was ordered for officials holding concurrent posts, within and beyond the capital.

translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the emperor learned that Zhao Xirui, associate administrator on the Zhongdu circuit transport commission, had often left unsigned the fiscal papers that mattered while in office, caring only to secure himself, and was demoted to prefect of Jishi.

translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the autumn hunt began.

translations.literal: " Participation Councillor Ma Huidi said: "Even if we had their people they would be useless, and their land uninhabitable—perhaps this hardly warrants Your Majesty’s concern."
translations.idiomatic: " Participation Councillor Ma Huidi said, "Even with their people they are useless and their land uninhabitable—perhaps this hardly needs Your Majesty’s concern."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕亦知此類無用，所以毀其船筏，欲不使再邊境耳！」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I know too that such people are useless; I destroy their boats and rafts so they cannot trouble the border again!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I know such people are useless too; I destroy their boats and rafts so they cannot trouble the border again!"

sentences.zh: 十月戊寅，定職官犯贓同職相糾察法。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on wuyin, the law on mutual scrutiny among colleagues when officials commit embezzlement was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on wuyin, the law on mutual scrutiny when officials commit graft was fixed.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上謂宰臣曰：「西南、西北兩路招討司地隘，猛安人戶無處圍獵，不能閑習騎射。

translations.literal: On gengyin the emperor told the chief ministers: "The territories of the Southwest and Northwest pacification commissioners are cramped; meng’an households have no place to hunt in enclosure and cannot leisurely practice mounted archery."
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor told the chief ministers, "The Southwest and Northwest pacification commissioners’ lands are cramped; meng’an households have nowhere to hunt in enclosure and cannot keep up mounted archery."

sentences.zh: 委各猛安謀克官依時教練，其弛慢過期及不親監視，並決罰之。

translations.literal: Entrust each meng’an and mouke officer to drill them on schedule; those lax, overdue, or not personally supervising—all are to be punished by judicial beating."
translations.idiomatic: Let each meng’an and mouke officer drill them on schedule; those lax, overdue, or not supervising in person—all are to be beaten and fined."

sentences.zh: 」甲午，詔增河防軍數。

translations.literal: " On jiawu an edict increased the number of Yellow River defense troops.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiawu an edict increased the Yellow River defense troops.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，甯昌軍節度使崇肅、行軍都統忠道以討烏底改，不待克敵而還，崇肅杖七十，削官一階，忠道杖八十，削官三階。

translations.literal: On wuxu Ningchang Army defense commissioner Chongsu and campaign commander-in-chief Zhongdao, having gone to attack the Udige, returned without awaiting the enemy’s defeat; Chongsu was given seventy blows of the staff and stripped one rank, Zhongdao eighty blows and three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Ningchang Army commissioner Chongsu and campaign commander Zhongdao, sent against the Udige, came back before the enemy was beaten; Chongsu took seventy blows of the staff and lost one rank, Zhongdao eighty blows and three ranks.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲辰朔，定閔宗陵廟薦享禮。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on the jiachen new moon, the rites for offerings at Minzong’s tomb and temple were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jiachen new moon, the rites for offerings at Minzong’s tomb and temple were fixed.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「女直人中材傑之士，朕少有識者，蓋亦難得也。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Among Jurchen there are men of outstanding talent whom I have barely known—truly they are hard to find."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers, "Among Jurchen there are outstanding men I have scarcely met—truly they are hard to find."

sentences.zh: 新進士如徒單鎰、夾古阿裏補、尼厖古鑒輩皆可用之材也。

translations.literal: New jinshi such as Tudan Yi, Jiagu Alibu, and Nimuguci Jian and their like are all usable timber."
translations.idiomatic: New jinshi such as Tudan Yi, Jiagu Alibu, and Nimuguci Jian and their like are all fit for use."

sentences.zh: 起身刀筆者，雖用才力可用，其廉介之節，終不及進士。

translations.literal: Men who rise from knife-and-brush clerical work may have usable talent, yet their integrity never equals that of jinshi graduates."
translations.idiomatic: Men who rise from clerical work may have usable talent, yet their integrity never equals that of jinshi graduates."

sentences.zh: 今五品以上闕員甚多，必資級相當，至老有不能得者，況欲至卿相乎？

translations.literal: Today vacancies above the fifth rank are very many, yet one must match qualifications and rank; some grow old without obtaining a post—how much less reach chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: Today vacancies above the fifth rank are many, yet rank and qualification must match; some grow old without a post—how much less reach chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 古來宰相率不過三五年而退，罕有三二十年者，卿等特不舉人，甚非朕意。

translations.literal: From antiquity chancellors mostly leave office within three to five years; rarely does one hold it twenty or thirty years—yet you notably fail to recommend men. That is very much against my intent."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity chancellors mostly serve three to five years; rarely twenty or thirty—yet you notably fail to recommend men. That is far from my intent."

sentences.zh: 」上顧修起居注崇璧曰：「斯人孱弱，付之以事，未必能辦，以其謹厚長者，故置諸左右，欲諸官效其為人也。

translations.literal: " He turned to Daily Recorder reviser Chongbi and said: "This man is frail; entrusted with affairs he may not manage them, yet because he is careful, steady, and elderly I keep him at my side, wishing you officials would model yourselves on him."
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Daily Recorder reviser Chongbi and said, "This man is frail; put to work he may not manage, yet because he is careful, steady, and elderly I keep him close, wishing you officials would take him as your model."

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，以刑部尚書移剌子元等為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: " On xinhai Minister of Justice Yelü Ziyuan and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinhai Minister of Justice Yelü Ziyuan and others were sent to congratulate Song on the New Year.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左警巡副使鶻沙通敏善斷，擢殿中侍御史兼右三部司正。

translations.literal: On wuwu Left Police Patrol deputy commissioner Husha Tongmin, for sound judgments, was promoted to palace attendant censor and concurrent chief clerk of the Right Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Left Police Patrol deputy commissioner Husha Tongmin, for sound judgments, was promoted to palace attendant censor and concurrent chief clerk of the Right Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 庚申，立右丞相原王璟為皇太孫。

translations.literal: On gengshen Right Chief Councillor Prince of Yuan Jing was established as imperial great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Right Chief Councillor Prince of Yuan Jing was made imperial great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上謂宰臣曰：「朕聞宋軍自來教習不輟，今我軍專務遊惰，卿等勿謂天下既安而無豫防之心，一旦有警，軍不可用，顧不敗事耶？

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor told the chief ministers: "I hear Song troops have never ceased drill; now our army devotes itself wholly to idling and pleasure. Do not think the realm is settled and need no precaution—if alarm comes and the troops will not serve, will affairs not fail?"
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor told the chief ministers, "I hear Song troops never stop drilling; now our army gives itself wholly to idling and pleasure. Do not think the realm is settled and needs no guard—if alarm comes and the troops fail, will affairs not collapse?"

sentences.zh: 其令以時訓練。

translations.literal: Order training at the proper season."
translations.idiomatic: Order training at the proper season."

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，上謂侍臣曰：「唐太子承乾所為多非度，太宗縱而弗檢，遂至於廢，如早為禁止，當不至是。

translations.literal: " On bingyin he told attendant ministers: "Tang crown prince Chengqian’s conduct was largely beyond measure; Taizong indulged him and did not check it, until he came to deposition—had he been restrained early, it would not have reached that."
translations.idiomatic: " On bingyin he told attendant ministers, "Tang crown prince Chengqian’s conduct was largely beyond measure; Taizong indulged him and did not check it, until he was deposed—had he been restrained early, it would not have come to that."

sentences.zh: 朕于聖經不能深解，至於史傳，開卷輒有所益。

translations.literal: I cannot deeply grasp the sacred classics, yet in histories and biographies, opening a volume always brings some gain."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot deeply grasp the sacred classics, yet in histories and biographies I always gain something from opening a volume."

sentences.zh: 每見善人不忘忠孝，檢身廉潔，皆出天性。

translations.literal: Whenever I see good men who do not forget loyalty and filial piety and who restrain themselves in integrity and cleanliness—all that comes from inborn nature."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I see good men who do not forget loyalty and filial piety and who keep themselves honest and clean—all that comes from inborn nature."

sentences.zh: 至於常人多喜為非，有天下者苟無以懲之，何由致治。

translations.literal: As for ordinary people, most delight in wrongdoing; if one who holds the realm does not punish them, how can order be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: As for ordinary people, most delight in wrong; if the ruler will not punish them, how can there be order?"

sentences.zh: 孔子為政七日而誅少正卯，聖人尚爾，況餘人乎？

translations.literal: Confucius in government seven days executed Shaozheng Mao—even a sage did so; how much more the rest of us?"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius in government seven days executed Shaozheng Mao—even a sage did so; how much more the rest of us?"

sentences.zh: 」戊辰，上謂宰臣曰：「朕雖年老，聞善不厭。

translations.literal: " On wuchen the emperor told the chief ministers: "Though I am old, I never weary of hearing what is good."
translations.idiomatic: " On wuchen the emperor told the chief ministers, "Though I am old, I never weary of hearing what is good."

sentences.zh: 孔子雲：'見善如不及，見不善如探湯。

translations.literal: Confucius said: “When you see good, hasten to it as if you cannot catch up; when you see evil, withdraw as from scalding water.”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, “When you see good, hasten to it as if you cannot catch up; when you see evil, withdraw as from scalding water.”

sentences.zh: '大哉言乎！

translations.literal: “How great these words!”
translations.idiomatic: “How great these words!”

sentences.zh: 」右丞張汝弼對曰：「知之非艱，行之惟艱。

translations.literal: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rubi replied: "Knowing is not hard; doing is what is hard."
translations.idiomatic: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rubi replied, "Knowing is not hard; doing is what is hard."

sentences.zh: 」以拱衛直副都指揮使韓景懋為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: " Commandant deputy of the Garrison Guard direct commission Han Jingmao was made envoy for Goryeo’s birthday.
translations.idiomatic: " Garrison Guard deputy commandant Han Jingmao was sent as envoy for Goryeo’s birthday.

sentences.zh: 以近侍局直長尼厖古鑒純直通敏，擢皇太孫侍丞。

translations.literal: Because Palace Attendance Bureau director Nimuguci Jian Chunzhi was forthright and penetrating, he was promoted to attendant of the imperial great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: Because Palace Attendance Bureau director Nimuguci Jian Chunzhi was forthright and penetrating, he was promoted to attendant of the imperial great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 己巳，獵近郊。

translations.literal: On jisi he hunted in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he hunted in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上謂宰臣曰：「朕方前古明君，固不可及。

translations.literal: On gengwu the emperor told the chief ministers: "Compared with the enlightened rulers of antiquity, I surely cannot reach them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor told the chief ministers, "Compared with the enlightened rulers of old, I surely cannot match them.

sentences.zh: 至於不納近臣讒言，不受戚裏私謁，亦無愧矣！

translations.literal: As for not accepting slanders from close ministers and not receiving private audiences from kin and consort clans—I have nothing to be ashamed of!
translations.idiomatic: As for refusing close ministers’ slander and kin and consorts’ private audiences—I have nothing to be ashamed of!"

sentences.zh: 朕嘗自思，豈能無過，所患過而不改，過而能改，庶幾無咎。

translations.literal: I often reflect myself: how could I be without faults? What I fear is faults uncorrected; if having faults one can correct them, perhaps one may escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: I often reflect: how could I be without fault? What I fear is fault left uncorrected; correct it, and perhaps there is no blame.

sentences.zh: 省朕之過，頗喜興土木之工，自今不復作矣。」

translations.literal: Looking at my faults, I have rather delighted in construction works; from now I will do so no more."
translations.idiomatic: Looking at my faults, I have rather delighted in building works; from now on I will do so no more."

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，上退朝，禦香閤，左諫議大夫黃久約言遞送荔支非是，上諭之曰：「朕不知也，今令罷之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jiashen, after audience the emperor withdrew to Xiangge Pavilion; Left Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue said relay delivery of lychees was improper; the emperor instructed him: "I did not know; now order it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiashen, after audience the emperor withdrew to Xiangge Pavilion; Left Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue said relaying lychees was wrong; the emperor told him, "I did not know; stop it now.

sentences.zh: 」丙戌，上謂宰臣曰：「有司奉上，惟沽辦事之名，不問利害如何。

translations.literal: " On bingxu the emperor told the chief ministers: "When offices serve things up, they only seek the name of fulfilling orders and do not ask what harm or benefit there may be.
translations.idiomatic: " On bingxu the emperor told the chief ministers, "When offices serve things up, they only want the credit for fulfilling orders and never ask what helps or harms.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗欲得新荔支，兵部遂于道路特設鋪遞。

translations.literal: I once wanted fresh lychees, and the Board of War then specially set up relay posts along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: I once wanted fresh lychees, and the Board of War set up special relay posts along the roads.

sentences.zh: 比因諫官黃久約言，朕方知之。

translations.literal: Only now through Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue’s words do I know it.
translations.idiomatic: Only now, through Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue, do I know it.

sentences.zh: 夫為人無識，一旦臨事，便至顛沛。

translations.literal: If a man is without knowledge, when he suddenly faces affairs he ends in distress.
translations.idiomatic: A man without judgment, when affairs suddenly fall on him, ends in distress.

sentences.zh: 宮中事無大小，朕常親覽者，以不得人故也，如使得人，寧複他慮。

translations.literal: That I personally oversee palace affairs great and small is because I do not have the right men; if I had them, why would I have other worries?"
translations.idiomatic: That I personally oversee palace affairs great and small is because I lack the right men; had I them, what else would I worry about?"

sentences.zh: 」丁亥，上謂宰臣曰：「朕年來惟以省約為務，常膳止四五味，已厭飫之，比初即位十減七八。

translations.literal: " On dinghai the emperor told the chief ministers: "In recent years I have only made economy my task; ordinary meals have only four or five flavors, and I am already weary of fullness—compared with when I first took the throne, [spending] is reduced by seven or eight tenths."
translations.idiomatic: " On dinghai the emperor told the chief ministers, "In recent years I have made economy my only task; ordinary meals have four or five dishes at most, and I am already weary of surfeit—compared with when I first took the throne, spending is down seven or eight tenths."

sentences.zh: 」宰臣曰：「天子自有制，不同餘人。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers said: "The Son of Heaven has his own regulations, unlike other men."
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has his own rules, unlike other men."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「天子亦人耳，枉費安用。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The Son of Heaven is also only a man—what use is waste?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The Son of Heaven is only a man too—what use is waste?"

sentences.zh: 」丙申，上謂宰臣曰：「比聞河水泛溢，民罹其害者貲產皆空。

translations.literal: " On bingshen the emperor told the chief ministers: "Recently I heard that the river flooded; people who suffered its harm have lost all property.
translations.idiomatic: " On bingshen the emperor told the chief ministers, "Lately I heard the river flooded; people who suffered have lost everything.

sentences.zh: 今複遣官於彼推排，何耶？

translations.literal: Yet now officials are again sent there for property assessments—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet now officials are sent there again for property assessments—why?"

sentences.zh: 」右丞張汝霖曰：「今推排皆非被災之處。

translations.literal: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rulin said: "The assessments now are all in places that were not disaster-struck."
translations.idiomatic: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rulin said, "The assessments now are all outside the disaster zones."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「必鄰道也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "They must be in neighboring circuits."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "They must be in neighboring circuits."

sentences.zh: 既鄰水而居，豈無驚擾遷避者乎？

translations.literal: Since they live by water’s edge, are there not those alarmed and displaced?"
translations.idiomatic: Living beside the water, were there not people alarmed and driven to flee?"

sentences.zh: 計其貲產，豈有餘哉！

translations.literal: Count their property—how could there be surplus!"
translations.idiomatic: Count their property—how could there be anything left!"

sentences.zh: 尚何推排為。

translations.literal: Why still property assessments?"
translations.idiomatic: Why still property assessments?"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「平時用人，宜尚平直。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In ordinary employment of men, straightforwardness should be prized."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "In ordinary appointments, straightforwardness should be prized."

sentences.zh: 至於軍職，當用權謀，使人不易測，可以集事。

translations.literal: As for military posts, stratagem should be used, so men are not easily fathomed—that can accomplish affairs."
translations.idiomatic: For military posts, use stratagem so men cannot easily read you—that is how affairs get done."

sentences.zh: 唐太宗自少年能用兵，其後雖居帝位，猶不能改，吮瘡剪須，皆權謀也。」

translations.literal: Taizong from youth could use troops; afterward though he sat on the throne he still could not change—sucking sores and trimming beards were all stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong could use troops from youth; even on the throne he never changed—sucking sores and trimming beards were all stratagem."

sentences.zh: 二十七年正月癸卯朔，宋、高麗、夏遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Year 27, first month, guimao new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, first month, on the guimao new moon, Song, Goryeo, and Xia sent envoys to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以襄城令趙渢為應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: On jiyou Xiangcheng magistrate Zhao Feng was made yingfeng Hanlin literary officer.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Xiangcheng magistrate Zhao Feng was made yingfeng Hanlin literary officer.

sentences.zh: 渢入謝，上問宰臣曰：「此党懷英所薦耶？

translations.literal: Zhao Feng entered to give thanks; the emperor asked the chief ministers: "Was this recommended by Dang Huaiying?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng came in to give thanks; the emperor asked the chief ministers, "Was this Dang Huaiying’s recommendation?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「諫議黃久約亦嘗薦之。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue also once recommended him."
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "Remonstrance Officer Huang Jiuyue also recommended him once."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「學士院比舊殊無人材，何也？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The Hanlin Academy compared with old times utterly lacks talent—why?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The Hanlin Academy has far less talent than of old—why?"

sentences.zh: 」右丞張汝霖曰：「人材須作養，若令久任練習，自可得人。

translations.literal: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rulin said: "Talent must be cultivated; if men are kept long in office to gain practice, men will naturally be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: " Right Vice Director Zhang Rulin said, "Talent must be nurtured; keep men long in office to gain practice, and you will get men."

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，如長春宮春水。

translations.literal: " On gengxu he went to Changchun Palace for the spring waters.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengxu he went to Changchun Palace for the spring waters.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥，還都。

translations.literal: Second month, on yihai, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，改閔宗廟號曰熙宗。

translations.literal: On yimao Minzong’s temple name was changed to Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Minzong’s temple name was changed to Xizong.

sentences.zh: 癸未，命曲陽縣置錢監，賜名「利通」。

translations.literal: On guiwei he ordered Quyang County to establish a mint office, granted the name "Litong."
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he ordered Quyang County to set up a mint, granted the name Litong.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上謂宰執曰：「朕自即位以來，言事者雖有狂妄，未嘗罪之。

translations.literal: On yiyou the emperor told the chief executives: "Since I took the throne, though memorialists have been reckless, I have never punished them.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the emperor told the chief executives, "Since I took the throne, though memorialists have been reckless, I have never punished them.

sentences.zh: 卿等未嘗肯盡言，何也？

translations.literal: You have never been willing to speak fully—why?"
translations.idiomatic: You have never been willing to speak your minds—why?"

sentences.zh: 當言而不言，是相疑也。

translations.literal: To have something to say and not say it is mutual suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: To have something to say and hold back is mutual suspicion."

sentences.zh: 君臣無疑，則謂之嘉會。

translations.literal: Where ruler and minister are without suspicion, that is called a fine assembly."
translations.idiomatic: Where ruler and minister are without suspicion, that is a fine assembly."

sentences.zh: 事有利害，可竭誠言之。

translations.literal: Where affairs have benefit or harm, you may speak with full sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Where affairs have benefit or harm, speak with full sincerity."

sentences.zh: 朕見緘默不言之人，不欲觀之矣。

translations.literal: When I see men who are silent and say nothing, I do not wish to look upon them."
translations.idiomatic: When I see men who stay silent, I do not wish to look on them."

sentences.zh: 」丁亥，命沿河京、府、州、縣長貳官，並帶管勾河防事。

translations.literal: " On dinghai he ordered that chief and associate officials of capitals, prefectures, districts, and counties along the river all concurrently supervise river defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " On dinghai he ordered chief and associate officials of capitals, prefectures, districts, and counties along the river all to concurrently oversee river defense.

sentences.zh: 己丑，諭宰執曰：「近侍局官須選忠直練達之人用之。

translations.literal: On jichou he instructed the chief executives: "Officials of the Palace Attendance Bureau must be selected from loyal, upright, experienced and perceptive men."
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he instructed the chief executives, "Palace Attendance Bureau officials must be loyal, upright, experienced, and perceptive men."

sentences.zh: 朕雖不聽讒言，使佞人在側，將恐漸漬聽從之矣！

translations.literal: Though I do not heed slander, if flatterers stand at my side, I fear I may gradually be steeped into heeding them!"
translations.idiomatic: Though I do not heed slander, if flatterers stand at my side, I fear I may gradually soak into heeding them!"

sentences.zh: 」上謂宰執曰：「朕聞寶坻尉蒙括末也清廉，其為政何如？

translations.literal: " The emperor told the chief executives: "I hear Baodi Commandant Mengkuomo is honest and clean—how is his governance?"

translations.idiomatic: I often recall that frugal custom and do not wish to waste recklessly; every palace officer and everyone granted food has a fixed ration.

translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the emperor went to Jinlian River.

translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the capital was shaken by earthquake.

translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised his filial piety and at once sent him home to tend her illness, to return when she had recovered.

translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Venus appeared in daylight.

translations.literal: Seventh month, on bingwu, Venus appeared in daylight and crossed the meridian.

sentences.zh: 壬子，秋獵。

translations.literal: On renzi the autumn hunt began.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the autumn hunt began.

sentences.zh: 九月己亥朔，還都。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the jihai new moon, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jihai new moon, he returned to the capital.

translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the emperor told the chief councillors, "In the prefectures and counties the spring waters passed through this year, the petty officials mostly did their work well—because I once rewarded and promoted such men, they all exerted themselves.

translations.literal: From this one sees that relying solely on responsibility and punishment is not as effective as using rewards to stir effort.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that relying solely on blame and punishment is not as stirring as using rewards.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥，宋前主構殂。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on yihai, the former Song ruler Gou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on yihai, the former Song ruler Gou died.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，祫享於太廟。

translations.idiomatic: On gengchen a joint seasonal offering was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor told the chief councillors, "Reading Tang history, only Wei Zheng remonstrated well; what he spoke of were all matters of state import, very much in the remonstrator’s proper form.

translations.idiomatic: Lately censors and remonstrators only pick out one or two petty matters, barely to fulfill duty, and never touch the realm’s great benefit and harm—do they know yet not speak?

translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor instructed the chief councillors, "People all take practicing the Way, honoring Buddhism, setting feasts, and reading sutras as merit; if I keep the people free of injustice and the realm at peace, is that not better than those things?

translations.idiomatic: He received the ministers’ homage in the Qinghe Hall and feasted again in the Shenlong Hall; princes and princesses in turn raised their cups to wish him long life.

translations.literal: The emperor was very merry and composed a tune in the native tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in high spirits and composed a tune in the Jurchen tongue.

translations.literal: Broadly it spoke of long rule upon the throne, advanced years, and distant thoughts on the weight of the dynastic foundation and the boundless trust of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly it spoke of long rule, advanced age, and a far-off sense of the weight of the dynastic foundation and the endless trust of ages to come.

sentences.zh: 以戒皇太孫，當修身養德，善於持守，及命太尉、左丞相克甯盡忠輔導之意。

translations.literal: It admonished the imperial great-grandson to cultivate his person and nurture virtue and hold fast to what he had, and charged Grand Marshal and Left Chief Councillor Kening to guide him with full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: It admonished the imperial great-grandson to cultivate virtue and hold firm to his charge, and charged Grand Marshal and Left Chief Councillor Kening to guide him with loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 於是，上自歌之，皇太孫及克甯和之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor sang it himself, and the imperial great-grandson and Kening harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor sang it himself, and the imperial great-grandson and Kening joined in harmony.

sentences.zh: 極歡而罷。

translations.idiomatic: They made merry to the full and then dispersed.

translations.literal: On wushen he ordered officeholders of sixth rank and above at court and fifth rank and above on the circuits to recommend jinshi already in service whose talent could fill the Hanlin Academy; they were to draft three pieces such as edicts, and those whose writing was rich and ample were to be appointed to posts in the Academy of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he ordered court officials of sixth rank and above and circuit officials of fifth rank and above to recommend jinshi already in office whose talent could serve the Hanlin Academy; they were to draft three pieces such as edicts, and those whose writing was strong were to be appointed to the Academy of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 應赴部求仕人，老病昏昧者，勒令致仕，止給半俸，更不遷官。

translations.literal: Candidates coming to the ministry to seek office who were old, ill, and dim of mind were compelled to retire, receiving only half salary and no further promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates coming to the ministry for office who were old, ill, and feeble of mind were forced to retire on half salary with no further promotion.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，幸壽安宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin he visited Shou’an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he visited Shou’an Palace.

sentences.zh: 四月癸酉，命增外任小官及繁難局分承應人俸。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on guiyou, he ordered increased salaries for minor officials on outside assignment and attendants in arduous bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on guiyou, he ordered higher pay for minor officials on outside assignment and attendants in arduous bureaus.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以陝西路統軍使孛朮魯阿魯罕為參知政事。

translations.literal: On dingchou Shaanxi Route commander-in-chief Boluolu Aruhan was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Shaanxi Route commander-in-chief Boluolu Aruhan became participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 癸未，命建女直大學。

translations.literal: On guiwei he ordered the founding of a Jurchen university.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he ordered a Jurchen university established.

sentences.zh: 五月丙午，制諸教授必以宿儒高才者充，給俸與丞簿等。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingwu, it was decreed that all professors must be veteran Confucians of high talent, with salaries equal to assistant magistrates and registrars.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingwu, it was decreed that every professor must be a veteran Confucian of high talent, with salary equal to an assistant magistrate or registrar.

sentences.zh: 戊申，宋使來謝弔祭。

translations.literal: On wushen Song sent envoys to thank him for the condolence mission.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Song sent envoys to thank him for the condolence mission.

sentences.zh: 七月辛亥，尚書左丞粘割斡特剌罷。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on xinhai, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhagewo Hutela left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on xinhai, Left Vice Director Zhagewo Hutela left office.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on jiazi the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the jiazi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛未，還都。

translations.literal: On xinwei he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上謂宰臣曰：「近聞烏底改有不順服之意，若遣使責問，彼或抵捍不遜，則邊境之事有不可已者。

translations.literal: On gengchen the emperor told the chief ministers: “I have lately heard that the Udige show signs of unwilling submission; if envoys are sent to rebuke them, they may resist and be insolent, and then border affairs may become impossible to stop.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor told the chief ministers, “I have lately heard that the Udige are showing signs of defiance; if envoys are sent to rebuke them, they may resist with insolence, and then border affairs may become impossible to stop.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗思之，抬徠遠人，於國家殊無所益。

translations.literal: I have often reflected that enticing distant peoples brings the state no real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I have often thought that enticing distant peoples brings the state no real benefit.

sentences.zh: 彼來則聽之，不來則勿強其來，此前世羈縻之長策也。

translations.literal: If they come, let them come; if they do not, do not force them—this is the long policy of past ages in keeping them on loose reins.”
translations.idiomatic: If they come, accept them; if not, do not force them—this is the old policy of loose reins.”

sentences.zh: 」參知政事孛朮魯阿魯罕罷。

translations.literal: ” Participation Councillor Boluolu Aruhan left office.
translations.idiomatic: ” Participation Councillor Boluolu Aruhan left office.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以山東路統軍使完顏婆盧火為參知政事。

translations.literal: On renwu Shandong Route commander-in-chief Wanyan Boluohuo was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Shandong Route commander-in-chief Wanyan Boluohuo became participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上謂宰臣曰：「用人之道，當自其壯年心力精強時用之，若拘以資格，則往往至於耄老，此不思之甚也。

translations.literal: On jiashen the emperor told the chief ministers: “In employing men, one should use them while they are still in their vigorous years, when mind and strength are keen; if one is bound by seniority, one often ends by employing them only in old age—how extreme a failure to think!”
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor told the chief ministers, “In employing men, use them while they are still vigorous, when mind and strength are keen; if one is bound by seniority, one often ends by employing them only in old age—what a failure to think!”

sentences.zh: 阿魯罕使其早用，朝廷必得補助之力，惜其已衰老矣！

translations.literal: Had Aruhan been used earlier, the court would surely have gained his help; it is a pity that he is already aged!”
translations.idiomatic: Had Aruhan been used earlier, the court would surely have gained his help; it is a pity he is already old!”

sentences.zh: 凡有可用之材，汝等宜早思之。」

translations.literal: Whenever there is usable talent, you should think of it early.”
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there is usable talent, you should think of it early.”

sentences.zh: 九月甲午朔，以鷹坊使崇夔為夏國生日使。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jiawu the new moon, Hawk Yard Commissioner Chongqi was made Western Xia birthday envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jiawu new moon, Hawk Yard Commissioner Chongqi was sent as Western Xia birthday envoy.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以安武軍節度使王克溫等為賀宋生日使。

translations.literal: On bingchen Anwu Army military commissioner Wang Kewen and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the imperial birthday.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Anwu Army military commissioner Wang Kewen and others were sent to congratulate Song on the emperor’s birthday.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，秋獵。

translations.literal: On yihai the autumn hunt began.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the autumn hunt began.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，還都。

translations.literal: On yimao he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月乙丑，京、府及節度州增置流泉務，凡二十八所。

translations.literal: Tenth month, on yichou, capital prefectures, circuit seats, and military commission prefectures added Running Spring offices, twenty-eight in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on yichou, the capital, circuit seats, and military commission prefectures added Running Spring pawn offices, twenty-eight in all.

sentences.zh: 禁糠禪、瓢禪，其停止之家抵罪。

translations.literal: Bran Zen and gourd Zen were forbidden; households that ceased them were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Bran Zen and gourd Zen were forbidden; households that practiced them were punished.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，尚書省奏擬除授而拘以資格，上曰：「日月資考所以待庸常之人，若才行過人，豈可拘以常例？

translations.literal: On yiyou the Department of State Affairs memorialized proposed appointments held back by seniority; the emperor said: “Monthly service tallies are meant for mediocre men; if talent and conduct surpass the norm, how can one be bound by ordinary precedent?
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the Department of State Affairs reported proposed appointments held back by seniority; the emperor said, “Monthly service tallies are for mediocre men; if talent and conduct surpass the norm, how can one be bound by ordinary precedent?

sentences.zh: 國家事務皆須得人，汝等不能隨才委使，所以事多不治。

translations.literal: State affairs all require the right men; you cannot assign duty according to talent, and so many matters go untended.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs all require the right men; you cannot assign duty according to talent, and so many matters go untended.

sentences.zh: 朕固不知用人之術，汝等務循資守格，不思進用才能，豈以才能見用，將奪己之祿位乎？

translations.literal: I truly do not know the art of employing men—you insist on seniority and grades and do not think to advance ability; is it that if ability were used, it would take your own salary and rank?”
translations.idiomatic: I truly do not know the art of employing men—you cling to seniority and grades and do not think to advance ability; is it that if the able were used, they would take your own salary and rank?”

sentences.zh: 不然，是無知人之明也。

translations.literal: If not, this is simply lack of discernment in knowing men.”
translations.idiomatic: If not, this is simply failure to know men.”

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰：「臣等豈敢蔽賢，才識不逮耳。

translations.literal: The ministers all said: “We would not dare hide the worthy; our talent and judgment fall short.”
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said, “We would not dare hide the worthy; our talent and judgment fall short.”

sentences.zh: 」上顧謂右丞張汝霖曰：「前世忠言之臣何多，今日何少也？

translations.literal: ” The emperor turned to Right Vice Director Zhang Rubi and said: “In former ages there were so many loyal remonstrators; why are there so few today?”
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor turned to Right Vice Director Zhang Rubi and said, “Former ages had so many loyal remonstrators; why are there so few today?”

sentences.zh: 」汝霖對曰：「世亂則忠言進，承平則忠言無所施。

translations.literal: ” Rubi replied: “In ages of disorder loyal words advance; in ages of peace loyal words have nowhere to apply.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Rubi replied, “In ages of disorder loyal words advance; in ages of peace loyal words have nowhere to apply.”

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何代無可言之事，但古人知無不言，今人不肯言耳！

translations.literal: ” The emperor said: “What age lacked matters worth speaking of? Only the men of old knew they must speak whatever they knew; the men of today simply will not speak!”
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor said, “What age lacked matters worth speaking of? The men of old knew they must speak whatever they knew; the men of today simply will not speak!”

sentences.zh: 」汝霖不能對。

translations.literal: ” Rubi could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: ” Rubi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊戌，以改葬熙陵，詔中外。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on wuxu, because Xiling was to be re-interred, an edict was issued within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuxu, with Xiling to be reburied, an edict went out to the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「凡修身者，喜怒不可太極，怒極則心勞，喜極則氣散，得中甚難，是故節其喜怒，以思安身。

translations.literal: The emperor told attendant ministers: "For anyone cultivating the person, joy and anger must not be carried to extremes; extreme anger wears on the heart, extreme joy scatters the vital breath—holding the mean is very hard, and so one should moderate joy and anger to think of securing the self.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told attendant ministers, "In self-cultivation joy and anger must not run to extremes; anger at the extreme wearies the heart, joy at the extreme scatters the breath—holding the mean is hard, so moderate joy and anger to keep yourself whole.

sentences.zh: 今宮中一歲未嘗責罰人也。

translations.literal: In the palace we have not punished anyone in a whole year.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace we have not punished anyone all year.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: " On gengzi Venus was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengzi Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 詔南京、大名府等處避水逃移不能複業者，官與津濟錢，仍量地頃畝給以耕牛。

translations.literal: An edict said that in Nanjing, Daming Prefecture, and other places where people had fled floods and could not return to their livelihoods, the state should give ferry and passage money, and still apportion land by mu and grant oxen for plowing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that families in Nanjing, Daming, and elsewhere who had fled floodwaters and could not resume farming be given travel subsidies, with land measured out by the mu and oxen supplied for the plow.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以河中尹田彥皋等為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: On jiachen Hezhong intendant Tian Yangao and others were made envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Hezhong Intendant Tian Yangao and others were sent to congratulate Song on the New Year.

sentences.zh: 戊申，上謂宰臣曰：「制條以拘於舊律，間有難解之辭。

translations.literal: On wushen the emperor told the chief ministers: "Statutes are bound by old laws, and here and there have wording hard to understand.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the emperor told the chief ministers, "Our statutes are cramped by old laws, and some phrases are hard to parse.

sentences.zh: 夫法律歷代損益而為之，彼智慮不及而有乖違本意者，若行刪正，令眾易曉，有何不可。

translations.literal: Laws are compiled and revised through the ages; where wisdom did not reach and they depart from the original intent, if we delete and correct them so the multitude readily understands, what cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: Laws are trimmed and added through the ages; where wit fell short and the text warps the intent, why not revise so everyone can grasp it?

sentences.zh: 宜修之，務令明白。

translations.literal: They should be revised to make them clear."
translations.idiomatic: Revise them and make them plain."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏重修上京禦容殿，上謂宰臣曰：「宮殿制度，苟務華飾，必不堅固。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized rebuilding the Imperial Portrait Hall at the Upper Capital; the emperor told the chief ministers: "In palace architecture, if one pursues ornament, it cannot stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: The offices proposed rebuilding the Imperial Portrait Hall at Shangjing; the emperor told the chief ministers, "Palace buildings that chase ornament will not endure.

sentences.zh: 今仁政殿遼時所建，全無華飾，但見它處歲歲修完，惟此殿如舊，以此見虛華無實者，不能經久也。

translations.literal: Renzheng Hall was built in Liao times and has no ornament at all, yet you see elsewhere repaired year after year while this hall stands as of old—by this one sees that the vain and showy cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Renzheng Hall was built under the Liao and has no flourish at all, yet elsewhere halls are patched every year while this one stands as it was—vanity does not last.

sentences.zh: 今土木之工，滅裂尤甚，下則吏與工匠相結為奸，侵克工物，上則戶工部官支錢度材，惟務苟辦，至有工役才畢，隨即欹漏者，奸弊苟且，勞民費財，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Today in earth and timber work the shoddy quality is worst of all; below, clerks and artisans band together in fraud and embezzle materials; above, Household and Works officials disburse funds and measure timber only to get the job done, so that sometimes when the work is just finished it at once leans and leaks—fraud, slackness, tormenting the people and wasting wealth, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s builders are shoddier than ever—clerks and craftsmen below collude and steal materials, Household and Works officials above hand out money and timber only to finish the job, so work is barely done before walls lean and roofs leak. Fraud of this sort wastes the people and the treasury—nothing worse.

sentences.zh: 自今體究，重抵以罪。

translations.literal: From now investigate thoroughly and punish heavily by law."
translations.idiomatic: From now on investigate and punish by law."

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，上謂宰臣曰：「朕近讀《漢書》，見光武所為，人有所難能者。

translations.literal: On gengxu the emperor told the chief ministers: "I have lately been reading the Book of Han and see what Guangwu did—what men find hard to do.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor told the chief ministers, "I have been reading the Book of Han and marvel at Guangwu—men find much of it hard to equal.

sentences.zh: 更始既害其兄伯升，當亂離之際，不思報怨，事更始如平日，人不見戚容，豈非人所難能乎？

translations.literal: After Gengshi had killed his elder brother Bosheng, amid upheaval he did not think to repay the wrong but served Gengshi as on ordinary days, and men saw no trace of grief on his face—is this not what is hard for men to do?
translations.idiomatic: After Gengshi killed his brother Bosheng, amid chaos he sought no revenge but served Gengshi as on any other day, with no grief on his face—is that not beyond most men?

sentences.zh: 此其度量蓋將大有為者也，其他庸主豈可及哉。

translations.literal: Such breadth of mind was surely preparing for great deeds; how could ordinary rulers compare?
translations.idiomatic: Such breadth was preparing for great deeds—how could petty monarchs compare?

sentences.zh: 」右丞張汝霖曰：「湖陽公主奴殺人，匿主車中，洛陽令董宣從車中曳奴下，殺之。

translations.literal: Right Vice Councillor Zhang Rulin said: "The Princess of Huyang's slave murdered a man and hid him in the princess's carriage; Luoyang Magistrate Dong Xuan dragged the slave from the carriage and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Councillor Zhang Rulin said, "The Princess of Huyang's slave killed a man and hid in her carriage; Luoyang Magistrate Dong Xuan dragged the slave out and executed him.

sentences.zh: 主人奏，光武欲殺宣，及聞宣言，意遂解，使宣謝主，宣不奉詔。

translations.literal: The princess memorialized; Guangwu meant to kill Xuan, but when he heard Xuan's declaration his anger dissolved and he ordered Xuan to apologize to the princess, and Xuan would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The princess complained; Guangwu meant to kill Xuan, but when he heard Xuan's bold words his anger faded and he ordered Xuan to apologize to the princess—and Xuan refused the command.

sentences.zh: 主以言激怒光武，光武但笑而已，更賜宣錢三十萬。

translations.literal: The princess spoke and inflamed Guangwu, yet Guangwu only laughed, then gave Xuan three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The princess goaded him further, yet Guangwu only laughed—and gave Xuan three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「光武聞直言而怒解，可謂賢主矣，令宣謝主，則非也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Guangwu hearing blunt words and letting anger go shows a worthy ruler, but ordering Xuan to apologize to the princess was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Guangwu was a worthy ruler to hear blunt speech and relent, but ordering Xuan to apologize was wrong.

sentences.zh: 高祖英雄大度，駕馭豪傑，起自布衣，數年而成帝業，非光武所及，然及即帝位，猶有布衣粗豪之氣，光武所不為也。

translations.literal: Gaozu was heroic and broad-minded, managed heroes, rose from common cloth and in a few years achieved the imperial enterprise—beyond what Guangwu matched, yet once he took the throne he still had the rough ways of a commoner, which Guangwu did not do."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was heroic and broad, ruled the bold, rose from common cloth to empire in a few years—beyond Guangwu—but once he held the throne he kept a commoner's rough edge, which Guangwu did not."

sentences.zh: 」癸丑，幸太尉克甯第。

translations.literal: On guichou he visited Grand Marshal Kening's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he visited Grand Marshal Kening at home.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙寅，以大理正移剌彥拱為高麗生日使。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingyin Court of Judicial Review director Yila Yangong was made envoy for Goryeo's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingyin Court of Judicial Review Director Yila Yangong was sent as envoy for Goryeo's birthday.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上不豫。

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor took ill.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，赦天下。

translations.literal: On gengchen an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔皇太孫景攝政，居慶和殿東廡。

translations.literal: On yiyou an edict ordered Imperial Great-Grandson Jing to act as regent and dwell in the eastern wing of Qinghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he ordered Imperial Great-Grandson Jing to govern as regent from the east wing of Qinghe Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以太尉、左丞相徒單克甯為太尉兼尚書令，平章政事襄為尚書右相，右丞張汝霖為平章政事。

translations.literal: On bingxu Grand Marshal and Left Chief Councillor Tushan Kening was made Grand Marshal concurrent Minister Director; Grand Councillor Xiang was made Right Director of the Department of State Affairs; Right Vice Councillor Zhang Rulin was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Grand Marshal and Left Chief Councillor Tushan Kening became grand marshal and minister director; Grand Councillor Xiang became right director; Right Vice Councillor Zhang Rulin became grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 參知政事完顏婆盧火罷，以戶部尚書劉暐為參知政事。

translations.literal: Participation Councillor Wanyan Boluhuo was dismissed; Minister of Revenue Liu Wei was made participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Participation Councillor Wanyan Boluhuo left office; Minister of Revenue Liu Wei became participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔尚書令徒單克甯、右丞相相襄、平章政事張汝霖宿於內殿。

translations.literal: On wuzi an edict ordered Minister Director Tushan Kening, Right Chief Councillor Xiang, and Grand Councillor Zhang Rulin to lodge in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he ordered Minister Director Kening, Right Chief Councillor Xiang, and Grand Councillor Zhang Rulin to keep vigil in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月壬辰朔，上大漸，不能視朝。

translations.literal: Year 29, first month, on renchen the new moon—the emperor grew gravely ill and could not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, on the renchen new moon of the first month, the emperor was gravely ill and could not hold court.

sentences.zh: 詔遣宋高麗、夏賀正旦使還。

translations.literal: An edict sent back the envoys dispatched to congratulate Song, Goryeo, and Xia on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the New Year congratulatory envoys to Song, Goryeo, and Western Xia recalled.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，上崩于福安殿，壽六十七。

translations.literal: On guisi the emperor died in Fu'an Hall at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he died in Fu'an Hall, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 皇太孫即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The imperial great-grandson took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial great-grandson ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 己亥，殯于大安殿。

translations.literal: On jihai the coffin lay in state in Da'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the coffin was placed in Da'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯朔，上尊諡曰光天興運文德武功聖明仁孝皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: Third month, on xinmao the new moon, his elevated posthumous title was declared Emperor Guangtian xingyun wende wugong shengming renxiao, temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinmao new moon, he was given the posthumous title Emperor of Illumined Heaven and Rising Fortune, of civil virtue and martial achievement, sage-bright and humane and filial, with temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 四月乙酉，葬興陵。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on yiyou, he was buried at Xingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on yiyou, he was buried at Xingling.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗之立，雖由勸進，然天命人心之所歸，雖古聖賢之君，亦不能辭也。

translations.literal: Eulogy: Shizong's enthronement, though by encouragement, was yet where Heaven's mandate and men's hearts converged—even ancient sage kings could not have declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Shizong's enthronement, though urged on him, was where Heaven's mandate and men's hearts met—even sage kings of old could not have refused.

sentences.zh: 蓋自太祖以來，海內用兵，寧歲無幾。

translations.literal: From Taizu onward the realm knew war year after year, with few years of peace.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu on the realm had known war almost without respite.

sentences.zh: 重以海陵無道，賦役繁興，盜賊滿野，兵甲並起，萬姓盼盼，國內騷然，老無留養之丁，幼無顧複之愛，顛危愁困，待盡朝夕。

translations.literal: Added to Hailing's lack of the Way, taxes and corvée multiplied, bandits filled the wild, armor rose everywhere, the myriad people looked on in hope, the country seethed, the old had no sons to support them, the young had no one to care for them, tottering in peril and want, awaiting death from morning to night.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's tyranny heaped taxes and labor on the land; bandits roamed; arms clashed everywhere; people watched and waited while the state churned—the aged without sons to support them, children without anyone to tend them—reeling in peril from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 世宗久典外郡，明禍亂之故，知吏治之得失。

translations.literal: Shizong had long governed outer circuits and knew the causes of turmoil and the gains and losses of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had long governed in the provinces and knew why chaos came and how officials won or lost.

sentences.zh: 即位五載，而南北講好，與民休息。

translations.literal: Five years on the throne and north and south were at peace; the people were given rest.
translations.idiomatic: Five years on the throne and north and south were at peace; the people rested.

sentences.zh: 於是躬節儉，崇孝弟，信賞罰，重農桑，慎守令之選，嚴廉察之責，卻任得敬分國之請，拒趙位寵郡縣之獻，孳孳為治，夜以繼日，可謂得為君之道矣！

translations.literal: Then he himself was frugal, exalted filial piety and brotherly duty, trusted reward and punishment, valued farming and sericulture, was careful in choosing prefects and magistrates, was stern in integrity inspections, rejected Ren Dedao's request to divide the state, refused Zhao Weichong's offering of counties as fiefs, and labored at government day and night—this may be called grasping the way of a ruler!
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, exalted filial piety and brotherhood, trusted reward and punishment, valued farming, chose magistrates carefully, inspected integrity sternly, refused Ren Dedao's petition to partition the realm and Zhao Weichong's gift of commanderies as fiefs, and governed tirelessly day and night—this was the way of a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，群臣守職，上下相安，家給人足，倉廩有餘，刑部歲斷死罪，或十七人，或二十人，號稱「小堯舜」，此其效驗也。

translations.literal: Then ministers kept their posts, high and low were at ease, families were provided for and men had enough, storehouses overflowed, and the Ministry of Punishments each year judged death cases—seventeen men, or twenty—and men called him "little Yao and Shun"; such was the proof.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers kept their posts; high and low were secure; households had enough and granaries were full; each year the Ministry of Punishments condemned seventeen or twenty men to death—and the age called him a little Yao and Shun. Such was the fruit.

sentences.zh: 然舉賢之急，求言之切，不絕於訓辭，而群臣偷安苟祿，不能將順其美，以底大順，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet his urgency in raising the worthy and his keenness in seeking counsel never ceased in his teachings, while the ministers rested easy in their salaries and could not extend his goodness to perfect order—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his urgency to raise the worthy and his hunger for counsel never left his words, while ministers clung to ease and salary and could not carry his virtue to full order—alas!
